headline: Microsoft has unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI chip, which it plans to make the main system for running AI in its products from 2027.
score_reason: Pool 8 lowered by 1: the chip was unveiled on 12 Oct, before the window; the facts are confirmed and the story is important.
importance_line: A cloud giant moving more AI work onto its own chips could lower what services such as Copilot cost to run over time and could weaken Nvidia's and AMD's hold on a major customer, but the 40% figure is Microsoft's own expectation and deployment has not started.
summary: Computerworld reports that Microsoft unveiled the Maia 300 on Monday 12 Oct 2026, its third-generation chip for running AI models, and Scott Guthrie, executive vice president for cloud and AI at Microsoft, said the company expects it to deliver 40% more tokens (the small pieces of text a model reads and writes) per megawatt of power than leading GPU-based systems, meaning chips from makers such as Nvidia. Microsoft plans to start deploying it after the turn of the year and to make the Maia family its primary system for running AI in its products from 2027, which, as The Verge noted, would make it less dependent on Nvidia and AMD.
notes: Event dated 12 Oct (before the 13 Oct window), so the score is lowered by 1 as instructed; not carried in the 13 Oct edition, so the coordinator may restore 8 if it wants this treated as new to readers. Short article (about 1,000 characters) but real text.
